verdict.left_looks: A tall, multi-tier pagoda-style build on a light grey stone-brick plinth. Dark brown wood walls with mixed plank and log-like textures, lit with a few lanterns or torches at the entry. Upper roofs are dark grey stone-slab with stepped, upturned eave tips (horn-like corner blocks) and a spire with a tall finial on top. Walls show a lot of recessed panels, patched and mixed materials, and some dark purple-speckled blocks. The lower tier is a wide box with a rectangular frame pattern; the upper tiers are more open, with posts and a skeletal lantern-like upper level. From the side the silhouette is busy and asymmetric, and the back reads as a stacked, uneven mass.
verdict.right_looks: A simpler stacked pagoda-like build on a grey stone-brick plinth. Dark brown brick-textured walls, mostly solid with evenly spaced window openings and a centered door on the front. Roofs are brown stepped slabs with overhanging eaves; the tower above has a small lantern with open windows and a thin antenna spire. From the side the mass steps up on a sloped, stair-stepped roof that rises from the front to a boxy tower. The back is a long solid wall with a few small windows. Overall it is cleaner, more uniform, with fewer small details, and the roof forms are clear and continuous.
verdict.why: The left build has far more readable character: distinct tiered roofs with upturned eave horns, a spire, and layered details that make it read instantly as a pagoda, while the right build reads as a plainer stepped tower whose roof forms are cleaner but less distinctive; the left's busier detail is deliberate style, not damage, so it wins on street impression even though the right is tidier in construction.
